en: Of all people upon the earth,
I say let every one come.
If, after hearing it, through some mishap,
They should happen not to come,
Let them see Kökötöy's red banner
With its golden finial above their yurts.
From hollows where no maiden has been seen,
Let not one soul remain;
From the bends and uplands,
Let no people remain without seeing it.
Say they must come to this feast of mine;
If they do not come to this feast of mine—
If he does not heed my words,
If he regards me with hostility,
I will seize the black banner,
And cast his people into turmoil!
Say that Bokmurun, Kökötöy's son,
Has camped at a suitable place;
Say that Kökötöy's countless riches
Sprouted like grass in spring.
The four corners of the world,
After his noble father died,
Have strength to wait four years.
Let every khan who hears the news come;
From the seven ages of the earth,
Let every living soul covering the land come!"
After Bokmurun had said this,
Baymyrza rose and spoke:
"Summon the four corners
All around the world.
If you do not act with princely dignity,
Summon all the peoples with elders,
Every one of them,
And do not behave like a child.
I know the people
Of the Kara Khitai and Manchus.
There are the people of Kakan-Chyn;
When all their tribes gather,
They have a custom of shedding blood.
There is ill-minded Zholoy,
And the formidable, vengeful Kongurbay;
They are enemies who will clash with us.
May infidels as numerous as cow hairs
Bring no trouble upon us.
After gorging on your feast,
Bokmurun, think of this:
May they not cast hellish torment
Upon your head, small as a button.
The man who gives the feast bears blame;
The man who gives the feast bears sin.
If your descent is low,
If the grass grows upward,
If the infidel peoples are many,
If what you rely on is like iron,
May none say that wretched Bokmurun,
Kökötöy's son, let infidels
Plunder Kökötöy's great wealth
When he offered the memorial feast.
This conduct of yours is arrogance;
Be firm and gather the people.
Do not offer a feast and have
This little band of Muslims beaten—
That is the mark of conceit.
Do not have this handful of Muslims
Plundered by the Kara Kalmyks and Manchus
Till only red tent-poles remain;
Mind their drunkenness and act!
The hero Manas is in Talas;
Bokmurun, you are twelve;
Find proper measure and act!"
When Baymyrza had said this,
Bokmurun rose and said:
"Baymyrza, rich man's son, bald fool,
Your camp is a difficult ravine, princely bald fool.
Your mount is a lone colt, princely bald fool;
What you drink is black tea, princely bald fool!
Mind your own feast, bald fool;
Clench your backside and take the road, bald fool!
I will not let you near my feast, bald fool;
I will not make you a burden on my head, bald fool!
You appeared as an enemy to my feast, bald fool;
Go away, do not come near me, bald fool!
Do not camp as though you were a great host, bald fool;
Do not swell the crowd here, bald fool!"
Thus Bokmurun,
Stamped upon the ground he walked,
Scolded Baymyrza,
Pounded the earth and raised dust,
And had his seven thousand attendants
Drive the swift horse Maaniker
Out from among the herd.
Kökötöy's Maaniker,
A swift horse surpassing a tulpar,
For a dead man's memorial feast
That stirred all the multitude—
The cause of Bokmurun's commotion.
Ah, the creature Maaniker,
A peerless one born among horses,
His form unlike other livestock.
He raced with flying birds;
The belly flesh from which fat is taken
Drew back, sleek,
And clung to his bones.
He did not panic at a battle cry;
In the darkness of the moon,
He never misplaced a single step.
He sprang apart at the sound of tumult;
Though there were countless hosts,
His qualities as a tulpar showed.
When he passed, the black earth
Split apart with a groan.
Were he not called a creature with feet,
He seemed to possess wings.
Unless his reins were held within a handspan,
He would not be taken by a determined foe;
Unless some wretched mishap struck,
He would not let fire touch his tail.
Unless a shot pierced his chest,
Unless a bullet went astray,
He would not let his rider fall to the foe.
The consummate swift horse Maaniker—
The wind could not catch his trot;
No beast could match his stride.
Unless his reins were gathered tight,
He shimmered like a flying bird,
And across deserts forty days wide
Shimmered like a cloud.
Though the desert were forty days wide,
He never once drank water.
The farther he ran, the longer his stride;
His eyes reddened like a spirit's.
Kökötöy's Maaniker—
A primeval dark-bay racehorse,
With sieve-like lungs and copper wings.
He never slipped from a height,
And was in no way inferior
To an ibex stepping upon rock.
Going to summon the peoples,
Ah, my colt, young Aydar,
Should you meet a desolate desert,
Do not let yourself race across it.
Do not wholly loosen his mouth,
Lest you fly over his back!
Take six swift horses;
Take a letter broad as a palm.
Travel the horse-road,
And roam the whole wide world,
Giving the news.
I shall tell you the peoples' order;
Hey, young Aydar, come here.
Behind that hunched mountain,
On the sun-facing brow,
At the lower foot of the pass,
This side of Old Turpan,
Beyond Wide Barbar,
Along the Lop River,
Where camels calve in the sand,
Who yield their companions to no one,
Are never sated by begging and consuming,
And never relinquish their greed,
Who, driven in darkness,
Prowl like lions—
With red whips and blue spears,
There is another people equal to the Kyrgyz:
There are the renowned Oygut people,
And their blessed khan;
Dwelling along the Lop River,
There is also one called Karacha.
Tell him to come to my feast
And see this spectacle!
If he does not come to my feast,
If he does not see this spectacle,
Tell him to behold Kökötöy's red banner with its golden crescent
From atop his own house!
Tell him to braid his daughters' hair
Into five forelocks!
When you travel onward from there,
Turning toward the sunset,
There is a city named Khotan.
There is Jügörü of Khotan,
Another great champion.
There is God's wrath in its water;
Do not weaken from drinking its water.
To Jügörü of Khotan,
Tell this news:
For Kökötöy's memorial feast,
Let him tether his swift horses
To bring and race;
Let him prepare his champions
To come and wrestle.
For my father's memorial feast,
I will slaughter a thousand black male camels;
I will slaughter a thousand black blaze-faced mares.
I will stake possessions of solid gold.
Give Jügörü my greetings;
Tell him to come to my feast
And see this spectacle!
If he does not come to my feast,
If he does not see this spectacle,
Tell him to behold Kökötöy's countless host
From atop his own house.
As booty for Bokmurun,
Tell him to braid his daughters' hair
Into five forelocks!
Tell him to come quickly,
Without making strife or quarrel!
On the left-hand side,
At the edge of the endless desert,
Among the rough, broken ridges,
Upon a gaping promontory,
There is the famed land of Yarkand.
Dwelling in that Yarkand
Is the campaigning champion.
Tell Khan Zhortuulchu to gather his people
And come;
Let him not leave his old men behind,
And let him bring his children riding
As usual upon their packsaddles.
Skirting the hot desert,
Let him come properly to my feast,
Having shod his tulpars.
Tell him to come to my feast
And see this spectacle.
If he does not come to my feast,
If he does not see this spectacle,
I will raid and destroy his people;
I will leave his donkey braying in the ravine.
If he fails to come in his turn,
This is how I will settle his account.
Tell every people you see without fail.
When you travel farther,
Covering ground without sparing your horse,
In the city of Wide Urgench,
In the villages of broad Afghanistan,
Tell their Khan Akun,
And tell all the peoples you see there.
Say that Bokmurun, Kökötöy's son,
Has camped at Üch-Karkyra;
Say that Kökötöy's great wealth
Has filled the face of the earth;
Say that Kökötöy's great feast
Has reached the time to be given!
Give Khan Akun my greetings;
Tell him to come to my feast.
If he does not come to my feast,
The clamorous shooting,
The struggle that cannot be healed—
Tell him to behold them from atop his house.
Tell him to surrender his beautiful daughter
As booty, without begrudging her!
Go no farther; turn back this way,
And return directly from that place.
With red banners and blue spears,
Let not one Kyrgyz remain behind.
When you head straight on from there,
You come to a place called Chambyl-Bel.
